proof_summary: Take the composite squarefree number \(n=3\cdot37\cdot43\cdot42307\cdot116341=23492890653051\).  For squarefree \(n\), the divisor-sum formula for Pillai’s function gives \(P(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}(2p-1)\), and here this product is \(610815156979325=26n-1\), so \(n\mid P(n)+1\) and the defining gcd is \(n\), yielding the counterexample.
